query: Which method can be used for concurrent strength–ductility improvement, and why?

generation.hypothesis: The eutectic alloy concept can be used for concurrent strength-ductility improvement in high-entropy alloys (HEAs).
generation.intervention: Proposed design strategy using eutectic concept for HEAs
generation.conditions: Room temperature and elevated temperatures up to 700°C
generation.mechanism: To tackle these problems, here we proposed a novel strategy to design HEAs using the eutectic alloy concept, i.e. to achieve a microstructure composed of alternating soft fcc and hard bcc phases.
generation.predicted_outcome: Unprecedented combination of high fracture strength and high ductility
generation.boundary: Limited to the specific composition and processing conditions of the AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanisms by which the eutectic alloy concept improves strength and ductility are not fully understood and may depend on the specific composition and processing conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the mechanical properties of HEAs designed using the eutectic alloy concept with those of traditional HEAs
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the eutectic alloy concept does not result in a significant improvement in strength and ductility compared to traditional HEAs, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Intervention effect. Base system: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (as-cast). Intervention: Compared against NiAl and NiAl/Cr(Mo) eutectic alloys. Processing: Comparison of mechanical properties data from literature and current study. Test conditions: Room temperature and elevated temperatures up to 700°C. Property change: EHEA exhibited much higher fracture strength and simultaneously much higher ductility at room temperature compared to NiAl or NiAl/Cr(Mo) eutectic alloys. Evidence: measured. Quote: "compared to NiAl or NiAl/Cr(Mo) eutectic alloys, the EHEA exhibited a much higher fracture strength, and more importantly, a simultaneously much higher ductility at room temperature"

Intervention effect. Base system: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (as-cast). Intervention: Proposed design strategy using eutectic concept for HEAs. Processing: Design based on pseudo-binary multi-component alloy system, varying concentration of one element systematically. Structure change: Fine lamellar fcc/B2 structure. Property change: Unprecedented combination of high fracture strength and high ductility. Mechanism: To tackle these problems, here we proposed a novel strategy to design HEAs using the eutectic alloy concept, i.e. to achieve a microstructure composed of alternating soft fcc and hard bcc phases. Evidence: simulated. Quote: "To tackle these problems, here we proposed a novel strategy to design HEAs using the eutectic alloy concept"

Intervention effect. Base system: AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy (as-cast). Intervention: Evaluated potential for large-scale industrial production. Processing: Preparation of industrial scale ingot (~2.5 kg) using conventional casting with commercially pure raw materials. Structure change: Uniform organizations and compositions. Property change: High fracture strength and high ductility achieved without expensive processing routes. Mechanism: Using this new alloy design strategy, an industrial scale HEA with uniform organizations and compositions can be prepared by the conventional casting method in a low cost way. Evidence: measured. Quote: "an industrial scale AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 ingot of ~2.5 kg in weight was prepared"
